# Prikk uninstaller (Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7).
#
# Generated by `prikk-release-policy generate-installer` at release time and published as a
# release asset (never committed as a tracked .ps1 file) -- see docs/src/guide/install.md.
#
# Removes exactly what install.ps1 added: prikk.exe at its install directory, the marker file
# install.ps1 wrote (only when it changed PATH), the install folder itself if it is then empty,
# and the user PATH entry -- but only if the marker says install.ps1's own run added it. Leaves
# everything else alone -- nothing else Prikk creates (a repository's own .prikk directory, for
# example) is touched.
#
# Usage:
#   irm https://github.com/REPO_SLUG/releases/latest/download/uninstall.ps1 | iex
#
# If you installed with a custom PRIKK_INSTALL_DIR, set the same value here so this script knows
# where to look:
#   $env:PRIKK_INSTALL_DIR = "C:\custom\path"
#   irm https://github.com/REPO_SLUG/releases/latest/download/uninstall.ps1 | iex
#
# Windows installer/uninstaller handoff v1 Part 6a2 (review 0.54.0-step-3-part-6a-review-v1,
# condition C1): wrapped in one script block (`& { ... }`), the same fix and for the same reason as
# install.ps1 -- see that script's own comment for the citations (about_Operators's Call operator
# section and about_Scopes). This script never called `exit`, but its own working variables
# ($installDir, $binaryPath, $markerPath, ...) and $ErrorActionPreference were still assigned at top
# level, so they leaked into the caller's own session under the one-line `iex` form exactly the same
# way install.ps1's did.
& {
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

# C3: see install.ps1's identical line for why this is printed from inside the run itself.
Write-Host "prikk-uninstall: running under PowerShell $($PSVersionTable.PSVersion)"

# C2: see install.ps1's own comment above these same two functions for the full citations
# (RegistryKey.GetValue's default-expansion behavior, RegistryValueOptions.DoNotExpandEnvironmentNames,
# RegistryValueKind, and Environment.SetEnvironmentVariable's own signature taking no
# RegistryValueKind parameter). uninstall.ps1 removes only its own one PATH entry from the raw,
# unexpanded string and preserves whatever registry kind (String/REG_SZ or ExpandString/REG_EXPAND_SZ)
# the value already had -- the same principle this script already followed for *which* entry to
# touch (only the one its own marker says install.ps1 added), now applied to *how* the value itself
# is read and written back.
function Get-RawUserPathEntry {
  $key = [Microsoft.Win32.Registry]::CurrentUser.OpenSubKey('Environment', $false)
  if ($null -eq $key) {
    return @{ Value = ""; Kind = [Microsoft.Win32.RegistryValueKind]::String; Existed = $false }
  }
  try {
    $exists = $false
    foreach ($name in $key.GetValueNames()) {
      if ($name -eq 'Path') { $exists = $true; break }
    }
    if (-not $exists) {
      return @{ Value = ""; Kind = [Microsoft.Win32.RegistryValueKind]::String; Existed = $false }
    }
    $kind = $key.GetValueKind('Path')
    $raw = $key.GetValue('Path', "", [Microsoft.Win32.RegistryValueOptions]::DoNotExpandEnvironmentNames)
    return @{ Value = [string]$raw; Kind = $kind; Existed = $true }
  } finally {
    $key.Close()
  }
}

function Set-RawUserPathEntry([string]$Value, [Microsoft.Win32.RegistryValueKind]$Kind) {
  $key = [Microsoft.Win32.Registry]::CurrentUser.CreateSubKey('Environment')
  try {
    $key.SetValue('Path', $Value, $Kind)
  } finally {
    $key.Close()
  }
  Send-EnvironmentChangeBroadcast
}

# See install.ps1's own comment above its identical Add-Type block for the SendMessageTimeout
# signature citation and the PSTypeName idempotency-guard citation (Add-Type's own documentation).
if (-not ([System.Management.Automation.PSTypeName]'PrikkInstaller.NativeMethods').Type) {
  Add-Type -Namespace PrikkInstaller -Name NativeMethods -MemberDefinition @'
[DllImport("user32.dll", SetLastError = true, CharSet = CharSet.Auto)]
public static extern IntPtr SendMessageTimeout(
    IntPtr hWnd,
    uint Msg,
    UIntPtr wParam,
    string lParam,
    uint fuFlags,
    uint uTimeout,
    out UIntPtr lpdwResult);
'@
}

function Send-EnvironmentChangeBroadcast {
  $hwndBroadcast = [IntPtr]0xffff
  $wmSettingChange = 0x1A
  $smtoAbortIfHung = 0x0002
  $result = [UIntPtr]::Zero
  [PrikkInstaller.NativeMethods]::SendMessageTimeout($hwndBroadcast, $wmSettingChange, [UIntPtr]::Zero, "Environment", $smtoAbortIfHung, 5000, [ref]$result) | Out-Null
}

$installDir = if ($env:PRIKK_INSTALL_DIR) { $env:PRIKK_INSTALL_DIR } else { Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA "Programs\prikk" }
$binaryPath = Join-Path $installDir "prikk.exe"
$markerPath = Join-Path $installDir "path-added-by-install.marker"

$removedBinary = $false
if (Test-Path -Path $binaryPath -PathType Leaf) {
  Remove-Item -Path $binaryPath -Force
  $removedBinary = $true
  Write-Host "prikk-uninstall: removed $binaryPath"
} else {
  Write-Host "prikk-uninstall: no binary found at $binaryPath (nothing to remove there)"
}

# The marker's presence is the only signal this script trusts for whether *this installer* added
# the PATH entry -- a pre-existing entry the user had for an unrelated reason has no marker next
# to it and is left untouched, exactly as the handoff requires.
$removedPathEntry = $false
if (Test-Path -Path $markerPath -PathType Leaf) {
  # 0.55.0 step 1 item 5: a marker written by this version (or later) of install.ps1 carries its
  # own `created-path-value: true|false` line (`-match`, not an exact line comparison, so trailing
  # whitespace or a line-ending difference never turns a real match into a miss). A marker written
  # by an older install has no such line at all -- `$createdPathValue` is then `$false`, the exact
  # value every install before this one implicitly had, so an upgrade's own stale marker changes
  # nothing about how this script already behaved for it.
  $markerText = Get-Content -Path $markerPath -Raw
  $createdPathValue = [bool]($markerText -match 'created-path-value:\s*true')
  $rawPath = Get-RawUserPathEntry
  if ($rawPath.Value) {
    # Part 6a3 (review 0.54.0-step-3-part-6a2-review-v1, condition C1): wrapped in @(...), for the
    # same reason as install.ps1's identical split/filter above (see that script's own comment for
    # the full about_Arrays citation). This one happened to work today only by luck of `-join`, which
    # rejoins a bare scalar into a one-character-shorter string indistinguishable from a one-element
    # array's own `-join` output when $entries holds exactly the installer's own single entry -- but
    # relying on that is fragile, so it is fixed the same way for the same reason.
    $entries = @($rawPath.Value -split ';' | Where-Object { $_ -ne '' })
    if ($entries -contains $installDir) {
      # Same fix, same reason: `Where-Object` can unwrap to a scalar when exactly one entry survives
      # the filter (for example, uninstalling the one and only PATH entry) and $kept -join ';' on a
      # scalar still produces the right string by coincidence, but $kept should be an array on its
      # own terms, not by accident of what -join happens to do with a non-collection input.
      $kept = @($entries | Where-Object { $_ -ne $installDir })
      if ($kept.Count -eq 0 -and $createdPathValue) {
        # This install created the Path value from nothing, and removing our own entry leaves it
        # empty: delete the registry value entirely, restoring the pre-install state, rather than
        # leaving an empty value that did not exist before this install ever ran.
        $envKey = [Microsoft.Win32.Registry]::CurrentUser.CreateSubKey('Environment')
        try {
          $envKey.DeleteValue('Path', $false)
        } finally {
          $envKey.Close()
        }
        Send-EnvironmentChangeBroadcast
      } else {
        # Either other entries remain (kept, unchanged from before this item), or this is an older
        # marker that never recorded creating the value (the old behaviour: write it back, possibly
        # empty, never delete it).
        Set-RawUserPathEntry -Value ($kept -join ';') -Kind $rawPath.Kind
      }
      $removedPathEntry = $true
      Write-Host "prikk-uninstall: removed the PATH entry for $installDir"
    }
  }
  Remove-Item -Path $markerPath -Force
}

if (-not $removedBinary -and -not $removedPathEntry) {
  Write-Host "prikk-uninstall: found nothing to remove"
}

if ((Test-Path -Path $installDir -PathType Container) -and ((Get-ChildItem -Path $installDir -Force | Measure-Object).Count -eq 0)) {
  Remove-Item -Path $installDir -Force
}

Write-Host "prikk-uninstall: done. Repositories under .prikk are untouched -- delete them yourself if you"
Write-Host "prikk-uninstall: no longer want that history tracked."
}
